subject: Urgent: HarborTrust inference slowdowns on dedicated pool — exec approval requested for burst allocation
messages:
From: Sophia Wu <sophia.wu@harbortrust.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Alan Choi <alan.choi@harbortrust.com>
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: Performance spike on dedicated pool (production)

Vanessa —

We're seeing a sharp degradation in production inference since ~17:50 UTC. Symptoms: 
- 95th percentile latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s for our /v1/generate endpoint.
- 5xx rate climbed to ~3.8% over a 20m window.
- Our reserved qps shows saturation and many requests are being throttled despite no change on our side.

This is impacting checkout flows — converting requests are timing out. Attached is a short token histogram and the monitoring snapshot. Can Redwood take immediate action (routing to a fallback, temporary burst, or credits) while we investigate? We can jump on a call now.

Thanks,
Sophia Wu
Head of ML Platform, HarborTrust

Attachments: nn-token-histogram.csv (token counts), slo-latency-dashboard.pdf (screenshot)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
To: Sophia Wu <sophia.wu@harbortrust.com>, Alan Choi <alan.choi@harbortrust.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 18:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Performance spike on dedicated pool (production)

Sophia — thanks for the flag and the attachments. Sorry you're seeing this. We're escalating immediately. Quick plan: 
1) I'm asking Ops to enable a temporary burst on your dedicated pool and apply a routing policy to divert low-priority scoring to a smaller model variant.
2) We'll open a short-lived capacity allocation (expected +2 GPUs) for 12-24 hours while we stabilize.
3) David/Karthik will run diagnostics to confirm whether this is noisy neighbors, a token surge, or an autoscale regression.

@David / @Karthik — please add diagnostics and an ETA. Marissa (cc) — we need exec approval for a short burst allocation and a customer credit if the root cause is on our side.

Sophia — do you have a scheduled batch job or change around 17:30–18:00 UTC? Any new prompts or model updates?

I'll keep the thread updated.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Schedule: https://cal.example/vanessa

Attachments: draft-escalation-note.docx (internal note)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.example.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sophia Wu <sophia.wu@harbortrust.com>, Alan Choi <alan.choi@harbortrust.com>
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 20:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Performance spike on dedicated pool (production) — initial ops findings

Quick diagnostics snapshot (initial):
- Reserved-capacity telemetry shows a token spike starting 17:36 UTC originating from a handful of hosts tied to HarborTrust prod keys.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~35% in the same window (suspect cache-TTL regression after a patch on the runtime).
- No large routing changes on HarborTrust's side reported via their API keys (Sophia, can you confirm?).

Suggested immediate actions (we can implement within 45m):
- Enable a +2 GPU temporary burst on the dedicated pool for HarborTrust for the next 12 hours.
- Apply a routing policy: divert non-checkout traffic to model-v2-small (20–30% token reduction) and keep checkout on model-v2.
- Roll back KV-cache TTL to previous value as a canary on a few shards (will measure 95th pct).

I've attached ops usage CSV and the SLO snapshot. If exec approves the temporary allocation I will schedule the capacity change and watch metrics.

-David
David Kim | Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ops-usage-summary.csv, slo-latency-dashboard.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sophia Wu <sophia.wu@harbortrust.com>
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 21:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Performance spike on dedicated pool (production) — implementing mitigations

On it. Actions underway:
- Enabling burst +2 GPU now (allocating from spare pool). ETA ~30–45m to warm up images and KV cache.
- Applying routing policy to send scoring jobs to model-v2-small; will keep checkout traffic pinned.
- Rolling KV cache TTL back on 10% of shards as canary; will widen if 95th% drops.

I'll post back with a short live update once the burst is up and we see the error-rate trajectory.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | SRE Lead, Inference Runtime, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Sophia Wu <sophia.wu@harbortrust.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:54:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Performance spike on dedicated pool (production) — executive approval and next steps

Forwarding: I reviewed the ops summary and the customer impact. Approving: 
- Temporary burst allocation: +2 GPUs for 24 hours (use spare pool).
- Customer relief: 30% credit on the impacted hour window; CS to follow up on formal credit amount.

Required from the team:
1) Postmortem draft by EOD Wednesday (root cause, hit mitigation, permanent fix, timeline).
2) A short customer readout (15m) with HarborTrust tomorrow at 11:00 UTC to walk through findings and next steps. Vanessa to coordinate.
3) Ops: confirm whether KV-cache regression (runtime change) or a downstream customer batch triggered token spike — include telemetry evidence.

Sophia — we'll schedule the readout and own the remediation. Apologies for the interruption.

— Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
